mainTopic: Neighbors' rights over gutters, drain pipes, ladders, windows and projections
overview: The amud opens by testing the earlier explanations of our משנה, which says a gutter pipe (מזחילה) has a חזקה. Under the view that the field owner may build beneath the pipe, the גמרא asks what the gutter owner could object to. It answers that the gutter is built into his walls, and building underneath would weaken them. Next, רב יהודה quotes שמואל: if a roof pipe drains into a neighbor's courtyard, the courtyard owner can stop the roof owner from sealing it. רבי אושעיא and his father רבי חמא argue about this, and רבי ביסא, the grandfather, sides with רבי אושעיא. The גמרא then defines an Egyptian ladder as one with fewer than four rungs. It explains that the משנה defines the Egyptian window only so that רבי יהודה's disagreement with that definition makes sense. רבי זירא and רבי אילעא argue whether a neighbor can protest a window built above four אמות. The גמרא shows their argument is not about כופין על מדת סדום, and the ruling follows רבי אילעא. שמואל adds that a window made for light gets חזקה at any size. Finally, a new משנה begins about a projection (זיז) that sticks out at least a טפח, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How does the gutter rule fit the 'he may build beneath it' explanation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a מזחילה has a חזקה. That fits the first two explanations of the משנה, but under the explanation that the field owner may build beneath the pipe, it is unclear what the gutter owner could object to.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'A gutter pipe has a חזקה.' According to the first two explanations, that works well. But according to the one who explains the משנה as 'if he wants to build under it, he may build,' what difference does building underneath make to the gutter owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line in our משנה about the gutter pipe and tests it against the different explanations given earlier. It works with two of them but causes a problem for the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first two explanations are right (the field owner may cut the pipe or move it), then 'the gutter has a חזקה' simply means he may not cut or move a fixed gutter. But the third explanation says the issue is building underneath. If so, the gutter's חזקה would mean the field owner may not build under it, and it is hard to see how building underneath harms the gutter owner at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A gutter pipe running along the edge of the roof, fixed in place
An established right gained through use over time
Granted / It makes sense (opens 'this works, but...')
What difference does it make to him?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the מרזב (a spout that sticks out) with the מזחילה (a gutter fixed along the roof). The משנה treats them differently, and this question is only about the מזחילה.

phrases.english: We learned: "A gutter pipe has a chazakah."
Granted, according to the one who says
those two explanations, it is fine.
phrases.notes: These are the first two explanations given earlier, by שמואל and רבי חנינא.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
that if he wants to build beneath it, he may build,
what difference does it make to him?
phrases.notes: He means: why should the gutter owner care if someone builds under his gutter?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָנָךְ תַּרְתֵּי – שַׁפִּיר. אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the earlier explanations of 'המרזב אין לו חזקה' against the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the field owner may build beneath the pipe.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חזקה is only about building underneath, then the gutter's חזקה would forbid building under it, yet building there seems to cause the gutter owner no harm.

steps.title: A gutter built into the walls
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a gutter built into the building itself. The owner can object to building beneath it because that would weaken his walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a gutter that is part of the building, where he says to him: 'I don't accept this, because my walls will be weakened.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by narrowing the case: this gutter is built into the walls of the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this kind of gutter is part of the structure, building right underneath it can damage the owner's walls. That is a real harm, so his חזקה lets him stop the field owner from building there. This saves the third explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with... (narrows the case)
A gutter that is built into the building
I don't accept it / It is not okay with me

steps.whatToRemember: Under every explanation, the gutter's חזקה is real. Under the 'building beneath' view, it protects the owner from someone building under a gutter built into his walls.

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a gutter pipe that is part of the building,
where he says to him:
It is not acceptable to me that my walls will be weakened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by defining the case more narrowly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a gutter built into the walls
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Building beneath a gutter causes its owner no loss, so his חזקה would be meaningless.
steps.terutzMaskana: A gutter built into the walls would be weakened by building beneath it, so the owner can rightly object.

steps.title: The courtyard owner can stop the roof owner from sealing his pipe
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: if a roof pipe drains into a neighbor's courtyard, the roof owner may not seal it, because the courtyard owner has acquired the water just as the roof owner acquired the right to drain into the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If a pipe pours water into his friend's courtyard, and the roof owner comes to seal it, the courtyard owner can stop him. He can say: 'Just as you acquired my courtyard to throw water into it, I too have acquired the water from your roof.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts here. שמואל gives a rule about a roof pipe that drains into a neighbor's courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we think of the roof owner as the one with a right, the right to drain into the courtyard. שמואל says the right works both ways: the courtyard owner has gained a right to that water and may want to use it. So the roof owner cannot simply close the pipe.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a right built up through use can create a claim for both sides, not only for the one who started the practice.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A pipe that pours water into his friend's courtyard,
and the owner of the roof comes to seal it,
the owner of the courtyard can stop him,
because he says to him:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאַתְּ קַנְיָא לָךְ חָצֵר דִּידִי
phrases.english: Just as you have acquired my courtyard
for throwing water into it,

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי נָמֵי קְנֵי לִי מַיָּא דְּאִיגָּרָךְ.
phrases.english: I too have acquired the water of your roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's gutter rules to a related new teaching about drainage rights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The courtyard owner can stop the roof owner from sealing a pipe that drains into his courtyard, since he has acquired the roof water.

steps.title: A dispute about whether the courtyard owner can stop the pipe from being sealed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא says the courtyard owner can stop the roof owner from sealing the pipe. רבי חמא says he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רבי אושעיא says he can prevent it. רבי חמא says he cannot prevent it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports two אמוראים who argue about the case of the roof pipe draining into a neighbor's courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the roof owner may not seal the pipe because the courtyard owner has acquired the water. רבי אושעיא agrees that the courtyard owner can stop the sealing. רבי חמא holds that the courtyard owner has no such power.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said: introduces a dispute between אמוראים
He can prevent or block it

phrases.english: It was said: Rabbi Oshaya says: He can prevent it.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the courtyard owner. He can stop the roof owner from sealing the pipe.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama says: He cannot prevent it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a dispute about the case in שמואל's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אושעיא: the courtyard owner can stop the sealing. רבי חמא: he cannot.

steps.title: רבי ביסא rules that the courtyard owner can prevent it
steps.stepSummary: The question was brought to רבי ביסא, who ruled that the courtyard owner can prevent the sealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and asked רבי ביסא. He said to them: He can prevent it.
steps.whatsHappening: The dispute is taken to an older scholar, רבי ביסא. He sides with רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ביסא agrees with רבי אושעיא: the courtyard owner can stop the roof owner from sealing the pipe. This backs up שמואל's ruling.

phrases.english: He went and asked Rabbi Bisa;
he said to them: He can prevent it.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose view is correct: רבי אושעיא's or רבי חמא's?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The courtyard owner can prevent the sealing.

steps.title: Three generations of scholars compared to a threefold cord
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא applies the פסוק about a threefold cord to רבי אושעיא, his father רבי חמא, and his grandfather רבי ביסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא read this פסוק about him: 'And the threefold cord will not quickly be broken.' This is רבי אושעיא, son of רבי חמא, son of רבי ביסא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short side comment praising this family of three generations of Torah scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three people in the story are grandson, father, and grandfather. Torah learning held strong across all three generations, like a cord woven from three strands.

keyTerms.meaning: He applied a פסוק to him

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama read about him:
"And the threefold cord will not quickly be broken" —

phrases.aramaic: זֶה רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חָמָא
phrases.english: this is Rabbi Oshaya, son of Rabbi Chama,
son of Rabbi Bisa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side comment on the people involved in steps 4 and 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three generations of scholars are like a threefold cord that does not easily break.

steps.title: What is an Egyptian ladder?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that an Egyptian ladder has no חזקה and asks what such a ladder is.
steps.simpleTranslation: An Egyptian ladder has no חזקה. What is an Egyptian ladder like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה and asks for a definition. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says this ladder gives no חזקה, but it never explains what an 'Egyptian' ladder is. The גמרא wants to know exactly which ladder the rule covers.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'Egyptian' ladder: a small, movable ladder
An established right gained through use
What is it like? A request for a definition

phrases.english: An Egyptian ladder has no chazakah.
What is an Egyptian ladder like?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.

steps.title: Any ladder without four rungs
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי defines an Egyptian ladder as any ladder that does not have four rungs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי says: any ladder that does not have four rungs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ladder with fewer than four rungs is small and easy to move, so using it does not establish a right. A ladder with four rungs or more is not 'Egyptian.'

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
Any one that does not have four rungs.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An Egyptian ladder is any ladder with fewer than four rungs.

steps.title: Why does the משנה define the window but not the ladder?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line about the Egyptian window and asks why the משנה explains the window but leaves the ladder unexplained.
steps.simpleTranslation: An Egyptian window has no חזקה, etc. Why does the משנה not explain the ladder, yet it does explain the window?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה is inconsistent. It explained one term but not the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא just had to define the ladder by itself, because the משנה left it out. Yet the משנה does stop to define the Egyptian window. Why treat the two items differently?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why the difference?

phrases.aramaic: חַלּוֹן הַמִּצְרִית אֵין לָהּ חֲזָקָה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: An Egyptian window has no chazakah, etc.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא גַּבֵּי סוּלָּם דְּלָא מְפָרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: What is different about the ladder, that it does not explain it,
and what is different about the window, that it does explain it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא גַּבֵּי סוּלָּם דְּלָא מְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fact that the גמרא had to define the ladder by itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה should treat both items the same way: define both or define neither.

steps.title: The window's definition sets up רבי יהודה's disagreement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines the window because רבי יהודה argues about it in the later part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it wants רבי יהודה to argue in the later clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why only the window is defined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה disagrees about the window's definition later in the משנה. So the משנה first had to state its own definition, so that his dissent would make sense. No one argues about the ladder, so the משנה did not need to define it.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of the משנה

phrases.english: Because it wants to have disagree
Rabbi Yehuda in the later clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא בָּעֵי אִיפְּלוֹגֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּסֵיפָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the משנה is worded this way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed inconsistent for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The window is defined only to set up רבי יהודה's dissent.

steps.title: רבי זירא: a window's height decides חזקה and protest
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says a window below four אמות has חזקה and the neighbor can protest it. A window above four אמות has no חזקה and the neighbor cannot protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: below four אמות, he has חזקה, and the neighbor can protest. Above four אמות, he has no חזקה, and the neighbor cannot protest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a rule about larger windows based on how high they are built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A window below four אמות can establish a right. That is why the neighbor is allowed to protest when it is built. A window above four אמות establishes no right, so there is nothing for the neighbor to protest.

keyTerms.meaning: Four אמות, a measure of height

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rights. 'Has חזקה' is about the window owner's right. 'Can protest' is about the neighbor's power to object. For רבי זירא, the two go together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Below four cubits —
he has chazakah, and the neighbor can protest;
above four cubits —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה, וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְמַחוֹת.
phrases.english: he has no chazakah, and the neighbor cannot protest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about window height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Below four אמות: חזקה, and the neighbor can protest. Above four אמות: no חזקה, and the neighbor cannot protest.

steps.title: רבי אילעא: the neighbor can protest even above four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא agrees there is no חזקה above four אמות, but holds that the neighbor can still protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אילעא said: even above four אמות, he has no חזקה, but the neighbor can protest.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא disagrees with רבי זירא about high windows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a window above four אמות gives no חזקה. They argue only about the neighbor's power to protest. רבי אילעא separates the two: no חזקה, yet the neighbor can still object.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא links protest to חזקה: where there is no חזקה, there is no protest. רבי אילעא holds that the neighbor can protest even where there is no חזקה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ile'a said:
Even above four cubits —
he has no chazakah, yet the neighbor can protest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי זירא about windows above four אמות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Above four אמות there is no חזקה, but the neighbor can still protest.

steps.title: Is the dispute about forcing someone not to act like סדום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי זירא and רבי אילעא argue about whether we force a person not to act with מדת סדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about whether we force someone not to act like the people of סדום? One master holds we force him, and the other holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible explanation for the argument in Steps 11-12. It suggests the argument comes down to a bigger principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדת סדום means refusing to let someone benefit when it costs you nothing. רבי זירא says the neighbor cannot protest a high window, so he would hold we force people to give up this selfish behavior. רבי אילעא lets the neighbor protest, so he would hold we do not force people.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
We force (בית דין compels a person)
The selfish trait of סדום: blocking someone's benefit even though it costs you nothing

phrases.english: Shall we say that about forcing someone over the trait of Sodom
phrases.notes: The trait of סדום: "I lose nothing, you gain, but I still won't let you."

phrases.english: they disagree?
That one master holds: we force him,
phrases.notes: This would be רבי זירא, who says the neighbor cannot protest.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: we do not force him?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּכוֹפִין עַל מִדַּת סְדוֹם קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the רבי זירא / רבי אילעא argument by linking it to a general principle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רבי זירא and רבי אילעא really about כופין על מדת סדום?

steps.title: No: everyone forces, but here the neighbor really loses something
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees we force people, but a high window is different because the owner can stand on a bench and look in.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees we force him. But here it is different, because the neighbor can say: sometimes you will put a bench under yourself, stand up, and look into my home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the suggestion from Step 13. It explains that רבי אילעא never denied the rule of סדום. He simply holds this case is not a case of סדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדת סדום only applies when the other person loses nothing. Here the neighbor can claim a real loss: even a high window can be used to look in by standing on a bench. So רבי אילעא lets him protest, while still agreeing that we force people in true סדום cases.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אילעא does not hold that we let people act like סדום. He agrees we force them. He just holds this neighbor has a real loss, so the rule of סדום does not apply.

phrases.english: No; everyone agrees that we force him,
but here it is different,
because he can say to him:
phrases.notes: The neighbor is speaking to the person who made the high window.

phrases.english: Sometimes you will put a bench under yourself,
and stand and look in.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כּוֹפִין, וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the argument is about the general rule of כופין על מדת סדום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the neighbor loses nothing. In fact he can lose privacy if the owner stands on a bench.

steps.title: A real case is ruled like רבי אילעא
steps.stepSummary: A man came to רבי אמי with this case. רבי אמי sent him to רבי אבא בר ממל, who ruled like רבי אילעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבי אמי. He sent him before רבי אבא בר ממל, who said: rule for him like רבי אילעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to show how the law was decided in practice. The ruling follows רבי אילעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a neighbor may protest a window built above four אמות, even though it has no חזקה. This fits Step 14: the neighbor has a real concern that the owner might look in.

keyTerms.meaning: Act for him according to (rule like)

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows רבי אילעא: above four אמות there is no חזקה, but the neighbor can still protest.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a theoretical argument into a practical ruling.

phrases.english: A certain man came before Rabbi Ami.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁדְּרֵיהּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל,
phrases.english: He sent him before Rabbi Abba bar Memel.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עֲבֵיד לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי אִילְעָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: Rule for him according to Rabbi Ile'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling in the argument just clarified.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The law follows רבי אילעא: the neighbor may protest a window above four אמות.

steps.title: שמואל: a window made for light gets חזקה at any size
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a window made to let in light gets חזקה no matter how small it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: and for a light window, even the smallest size has חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds a new rule about windows. A window made to let light into a room gets חזקה at any size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The window discussion so far was about size and height. שמואל adds that for a window meant to bring in light, size does not matter. Even a tiny one gets חזקה, so if the neighbor did not protest, he cannot later make the owner close it.

keyTerms.meaning: Light (a window made to bring in light)
Any amount, even the smallest size
An established right to use something, gained because the neighbor did not protest

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
And for light,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כָּל שֶׁהוּא יֵשׁ לוֹ חֲזָקָה.
phrases.english: even any size at all, it has a chazakah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new rule about windows after the high-window discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A window made for light gets חזקה at any size.

steps.title: New משנה: a projection of a טפח or more has חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new case: a זיז, a projection sticking out from a wall over a courtyard, can gain חזקה if it sticks out at least a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A projection, up to a handbreadth, has חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts about a זיז, a ledge sticking out of one's wall over a neighbor's courtyard. This line opens the rule, and the משנה continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like windows, a projection can become an established right if the neighbor does not protest. The size line here is a טפח. The rest of the משנה, about smaller projections, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A projection or ledge sticking out from a wall

phrases.english: MISHNA: A projection:
